subject.title: [Task] Harden browser/search stack and evaluate Lightpanda

question: Should this broad task remain a single browser/search hardening program, or should maintainers split it into approved search-provider fixes, browser/Lightpanda backend design, and benchmarking/security tracks?
rationale: The current code has multiple related seams but no single implementation path; choosing a browser/search product boundary affects core APIs, config, security posture, benchmarking, and plugin ownership.

options.title: Split into scoped tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the coordination item, but require narrower maintainer-approved issues or PRs for search fixes, Lightpanda/external-CDP design, and benchmark proof before implementation.

options.title: Fold into existing browser issues
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/52662 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53763 as the canonical implementation paths and close or rewrite this issue after preserving the benchmark requirements there.

options.title: Keep as research-only
options.body: Limit this issue to a read-only evaluation matrix and require separate product/security approval before any runtime or config changes.

recommendation.title: Split into scoped tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the coordination item, but require narrower maintainer-approved issues or PRs for search fixes, Lightpanda/external-CDP design, and benchmark proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue spans browser plugin boundaries, core web tools, security defaults, and product scoping, and steipete has the strongest recent history across those surfaces.
